A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same V3 research, and their supplied text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, v1 refers to an appendix that is absent from its PDF, limiting comparison of earlier implementation details with v2's Appendices A-E.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on synthetic music and digit images, including retrieval, codebook interpretability and loss ablations in Tables 1-4.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments across five datasets, including retrieval, classification, speaker verification, unseen-style adaptation and ablations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the VQ encoder-decoder, mean pairwise distance statistics and four hinge-ratio regularizers, with unchanged Equations 1-13. Appendix B supplies implementation details without establishing a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The original synthetic digit and music tasks remain as PhoneNums and InsNotes. v2 adds SVHN, Sprites and Libri100, extending evaluation to natural digit images, animation actions and speech phonemes/speakers. It also evaluates previously unseen colors and instruments.

E2.justification: v2 adds beta-VAE to the retained retrieval comparisons, raw-input classifiers to the new probing experiments, and CNN classifiers to unseen-style adaptation. The earlier weakly and fully supervised methods are retained under EC2-VAE names, rather than being new baselines. Their rows are removed from the quantitative codebook-interpretability comparison.

E3.justification: Retrieval evaluation now measures both intended information and cross-factor leakage from each latent branch. New protocols include one-epoch linear probes, speaker verification using averaged embeddings and equal error rate, and 0/1/5/10-shot adaptation to unseen styles with different supervision and self-boosting conditions.

E4.justification: v2 adds unseen-style robustness experiments, latent recombination studies and SVHN/Libri100 error analyses. The SD and leave-one-loss-out ablations persist, moving from v1 Tables 2 and 4 to v2 Tables 13 and 14; they gain cross-factor retrieval measurements but lose codebook accuracy and cross-style dispersion columns.

E5.justification: v2 newly states that reported results average the three best-performing validation checkpoints. This adds an aggregation disclosure, not evidence of three independent runs. Neither version reports seed-based uncertainty or significance tests; the retained sigma metric measures cross-style disagreement.

E6.justification: Existing values change beyond percentage conversion: on music at K=12, MINE content PR-AUC changes from 8.5% to 56.4%, and V3 from 90.4% to 89.9% (v1 Table 1; v2 Table 2). v2 also adds substantial probing, verification, adaptation and qualitative results. These are revised reports, not established same-setting gains, because identical run and aggregation conditions are not documented.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, variability statistics and loss formulations in Equations 1-13 are retained. Appendix E adds conceptual discussion rather than new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: v2 makes superior few-shot generalization to unseen styles a central contribution, beyond v1's claims of disentanglement comparable to supervised methods. Its claimed empirical scope expands to audio, images and video, and the symbolic-emergence contribution explicitly requires semantic segmentations.

C2.justification: Appendices C and E add interpretations of digit and phoneme confusions and explanations connecting disentanglement with adaptation and symbolic interpretability. Section 5 newly distinguishes learning atomic symbols from learning their meanings or compositions. Existing segmentation and non-overlapping-content limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A-B newly document dataset construction and splits, preprocessing, network dimensions, optimizer and loss settings, codebook updates, hardware and training times. v2 also supplies a code repository link alongside the retained demo link. These substantially expand documentation; they do not establish that previously unspecified settings changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantial coverage of sequential disentanglement, including DSAE and its variants. Appendix E explicitly compares V3 with InfoGAN, DSAE and VICReg, distinguishing context dependence, sequence-level style encoding and interpretable symbols. This materially expands research positioning beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and contribution narrative are revised. Experiments are reorganized from separate dataset-centered accounts into shared dataset descriptions and evaluation objectives, while ablations and much qualitative evidence move into structured appendices. The discussion and implementation narrative are substantially expanded.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figures 1-2, restructures retrieval tables with cross-latent columns, and separates codebook results into dedicated tables. Earlier visualizations move into expanded appendix grids, accompanied by new dataset examples, recombination figures, confusion matrices and adaptation tables. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1's evidence is confined to two synthetic tasks with sparse implementation documentation. v2 substantially strengthens validation through real images and speech, animation, cross-factor leakage measurements and unseen-style adaptation, while supplying detailed reproducibility information. Its broad supervised-superiority claims still need qualification because Table 7 includes stronger label-assisted EC2-VAE results, and independent-run uncertainty remains absent. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and transparency.
